title: Protect the feeling when shipping
principle: Every late addition can dilute the feeling you fought for. Ship decisions should defend the emotional thesis of the piece.
procedure: Write the feeling in one sentence (calm authority, playful precision, etc.).
For each late request, ask: does this strengthen or dilute the feeling?
Cut or quarantine diluting requests into a later experiment.
Preserve silence/negative space that carries the feeling.
Final pass: remove one thing that doesn’t serve the sentence.
examplePrompts:
Feeling thesis: <one sentence>.
Audit these late requests: <list>.
Keep / cut / quarantine each with a one-line reason tied to the thesis.
End by removing one non-serving element.
promptWhy: Ties cuts to an emotional thesis.
tips: Process essays from van Schneider stress intention through to shipping.

workedExamples.title: Stakeholder sticker pack
workedExamples.before: Add badges, banners, and a second CTA ‘just in case’.
workedExamples.after: One CTA; extras quarantined; silence preserved.

workedExamples.title: Loud last mile
workedExamples.before: Marketing overlay breaks the calm layout.
workedExamples.after: Overlay redesigned to obey the thesis or cut.
workedExamples.body: Protect the feeling at the finish.

antiPatterns: Letting silence get filled by default.
